q: Rice's theorem in computability theory is the analogue of which dynamical systems result?
opts: The undecidability of nontrivial asymptotic properties of the universal Turing machine's orbits
exp: Rice's theorem: every non-trivial property of computable functions is undecidable. Dynamically: any non-trivial property of the 'orbit' of a Turing machine (does it halt? does it output an even number? does it have a fixed point?) is undecidable — an undecidability theorem about orbits.
